title: Sistem Informasi Stok Bahan Baku Berbasis Web Framework Laravel Pada Cafe 1/2 Kopi Tiam Sepakat
venue: Jurnal Komputer Teknologi Informasi Sistem Komputer (JUKTISI)
abstract_evidence: Builds a web-based raw-material stock information system for Cafe 1/2 Kopi Tiam Sepakat (Pontianak), whose inventory relied on manual ledger books causing recording errors, slow stock checks and risk of lost documents. The system uses Laravel and MySQL, developed with the Waterfall model, and includes item presets to prevent entry errors and an activity log (audit trail). Black-Box testing found all features working, and a UAT with 12 internal cafe respondents (1 executive, 1 branch head, 10 barista and kitchen staff; 5-point Likert) scored 531 of 565 points, which the paper reports as 94.63% ('very feasible'); note that 531/565 = 93.98%, so the reported percentage is inconsistent with the paper's own formula.
relevance: Bab 1 latar belakang (manual raw-material recording problems in cafes); Bab 2 penelitian terkait; Bab 3 (black-box + UAT evaluation precedent with barista/kitchen staff as respondents, comparable to our bar users); paper related work: inventory handled as standalone stock records, not deducted automatically from standard recipes as in our system. Quote the UAT result approximately (about 94%, 'very feasible') or note the arithmetic inconsistency.

title: The Implementation of PWA (Progressive Web App) Technology in Enhancing Website Performance & Mobile Accessibility
publisher: Badan Penelitian dan Pengembangan Sumber Daya Manusia Kementerian Komunikasi dan Informatika
abstract_evidence: Implements PWA features on a website (web app manifest, service worker registration and configuration, cache storage, specific Express.js routes) to overcome the inability to display pages offline and the cost of building native apps for each OS platform. Testing covered installation, evaluation of PWA criteria, performance, size of transferred resources and offline mode, measured with tools such as PWABuilder, Google Lighthouse, GTmetrix and Chrome DevTools (full text). The website could be installed and used on mobile and desktop devices and accessed offline or on unstable connections; the full text reports the Lighthouse performance score rising from 62 to 98 (LCP 2.8 s to 0.9 s, CLS 0.153 to 0.01) and GTmetrix from 63% (grade D) to 99% (grade A) after implementing the PWA together with several other optimizations, so the gains are not attributable to the PWA alone.

Cite it for the test procedure, not as proof that a PWA by itself improves performance.

title: Determining What Individual SUS Scores Mean: Adding an Adjective Rating Scale
abstract_evidence: The authors added a seven-point adjective-anchored Likert item ('Worst Imaginable' to 'Best Imaginable') as an eleventh question to nearly 1,000 SUS surveys to learn how a numeric SUS score translates into an absolute judgment of usability. The adjective ratings correlated very strongly with SUS scores (r = 0.822), and the authors propose the adjective scale to help practitioners interpret individual SUS scores and explain them to non-human-factors professionals. In the full text (Table 3, n = 959) the mean SUS score per adjective was: Worst Imaginable 12.5, Awful 20.3, Poor 35.7, OK 50.9, Good 71.4, Excellent 85.5, Best Imaginable 90.9, and Figure 4 relates the adjectives to acceptability ranges and a school-grade scale. The authors caution that 'OK' had the highest variance of the seven adjectives and may wrongly suggest an acceptable product (they suggest 'fair' or 'so-so' instead), and that the letter-grade mapping so far rests on anecdotal evidence.
relevance: Bab 3 metode analisis dan Bab 4 pembahasan: mapping the PWA's mean SUS score to an adjective rating, grade scale and acceptability range; paper evaluation (interpretation of SUS). Foundational non-DOI journal article kept because the SUS interpretation used in the thesis and the paper depends on it. When reporting the adjective, state the authors' own caveat that 'OK' can wrongly imply acceptability (p. 120).

title: Brew temperature, at fixed brew strength and extraction, has little impact on the sensory profile of drip brew coffee
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract_evidence: Drip coffee was brewed to specific TDS and percent-extraction (PE) targets spanning the classic Coffee Brewing Control Chart at 87, 90 or 93 °C, adjusting grind size and brew time to reach the targets. The authors conclude that brew temperature is only one of several parameters affecting extraction dynamics and that the sensory profile is governed by TDS and PE rather than brew temperature, at least over the range of temperatures tested.

title: Titratable Acidity, Perceived Sourness, and Liking of Acidity in Drip Brewed Coffee
abstract_evidence: Sour perception and acidity liking of drip coffee were assessed over a wide range of brew strengths and extraction yields at three roast levels and three brew temperatures (87, 90 and 93 °C). Perceived sour intensity correlated weakly with pH but strongly with titratable acidity, and higher titratable acidity increased 'too much acidity' ratings and affected consumer liking and segmentation. Titratable acidity was linearly correlated with TDS under all conditions studied, indicating TDS is a good proxy for titratable acidity.

title: Sensory Analysis of Full Immersion Coffee: Cold Brew Is More Floral, and Less Bitter, Sour, and Rubbery Than Hot Brew
abstract_evidence: A 3×3×3 factorial study (three origins/post-harvest methods, three roast levels, brew temperatures of 4, 22 and 92 °C) brewed full-immersion coffee to equilibrium, diluted all brews to 2% TDS and served them at 4 °C. title: Basic Kitchen and Food Service Management

title: SUS: A 'Quick and Dirty' Usability Scale
abstract_evidence: Brooke argues that usability has no absolute meaning and can only be defined relative to a context of use (intended users, tasks and environment; ISO 9241-11 effectiveness, efficiency and satisfaction), yet industrial evaluation needs quick, low-cost, general measures for comparing systems. The chapter describes the System Usability Scale (SUS), a ten-item Likert scale giving a global view of subjective usability, whose items were selected from a pool of 50 candidates and alternate between positive and negative statements to avoid response bias. title: Asymptotic Optimality of Base-Stock Policies for Perishable Inventory Systems
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
abstract_evidence: The paper studies periodic-review perishable inventory systems with a fixed product lifetime, lost sales or backlogging, and the objective of minimising long-run average holding, penalty and outdating cost; the optimal policy is notoriously complex and computationally intractable. For the classic system, it proves that a simple base-stock policy, which raises total inventory to a constant level each period, is asymptotically optimal when product lifetime, demand population size, unit penalty cost or unit outdating cost becomes large, with the optimality gap vanishing exponentially fast in the first two. The results extend to LIFO or arbitrary issuance and to backlogging systems with positive lead times, and a numerical study shows how base-stock policies perform.
relevance: Bab 2 landasan teori (kebijakan persediaan bahan mudah rusak): theoretical justification for the order-up-to (base-stock) form of Takar's restock recommendation for perishable cafe ingredients such as milk or pastries. The exact optimal perishable policy is computationally intractable, but a simple base-stock policy is asymptotically optimal as product lifetime, demand population size, or unit penalty/outdating cost grows. It does not validate Takar's specific safety-stock or reorder-point parameters. Paper: method justification (restock recommendations).

title: Performance of recommender algorithms on top-n recommendation tasks
venue: Proceedings of the fourth ACM conference on Recommender systems
abstract_evidence: Explains that commercial systems usually show 'best bet' recommendations without the predicted rating values (the top-N recommendation task), that methodologies based on error metrics such as RMSE are not a natural fit for evaluating this task, and that top-N performance can be measured directly with accuracy metrics such as precision/recall. The authors also offer variants of two collaborative-filtering algorithms that significantly outperform the other algorithms on the top-N task.

abstract_evidence: Presents item-based top-N recommendation algorithms that first compute similarities between items and then combine them to score the similarity between a basket of items and each candidate item; on eight real datasets they are up to two orders of magnitude faster than user-neighbourhood collaborative filtering with comparable or better quality. title: SQLite: past, present, and future
source_checked: project check 2026-09-30: backend\app\config.py (database_url sqlite:///backend/data/takar.db); backend\app\models.py (18 __tablename__ entries)
abstract_evidence: The paper reports that in the two decades after its initial release SQLite has become the most widely deployed database engine in existence, and names several factors likely responsible for its ubiquity: its in-process design, standalone codebase, extensive test suite and cross-platform file format. abstract_evidence: Tutorial-style review arguing that ML researchers often adopt flawed forecast-evaluation practices, and giving best practices for data partitioning, error calculation, statistical testing and the choice of error measures according to data characteristics. The full text distinguishes fixed-origin from rolling-origin evaluation (citing Tashman 2000): with a rolling origin the horizon is fixed while the origin moves, creating several test periods and allowing refits with new data (also called time-series cross-validation), recommended when enough data are available. Its Table 8 defines WAPE as the sum of absolute errors over the horizon divided by the sum of absolute actuals, and it warns that on intermittent series per-step percentage errors divide by zero and benchmark-scaled errors fail when the benchmark (e.g. naive) makes exact zero errors.
relevance: Bab 2 landasan teori and Bab 3 metode (SPEC 7.3): peer-reviewed support for the 8-origin rolling-origin backtest with refits on data up to each origin, the WAPE formula used for model selection, and the caveats of MAPE and MASE on item-level cafe series with many zero-sales days (26.6 % of the Maven store x product daily cells, computed here). Paper method; complements hyndman2021forecasting and hyndman2006another.
topic: rolling-origin forecast evaluation and WAPE definition
note: Crossref 'issued' 2022-12-02 (online first); print issue 37(2), March 2023. Open access (CC BY 4.0).

Crossref and OpenAlex match title, 3 authors in order, year 2022 (Crossref issued 2022-12-02; published-print 2023-03), Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 37(2):788-832, journal-article; licence CC BY 4.0 (Crossref licence field and the PDF). abstract_evidence checked against the Crossref abstract and the open-access PDF: fixed vs rolling origin (Tashman 2000), tsCV/prequential naming, re-fitting with new data at each origin, 'a good choice with sufficient amounts of data', Table 8 WAPE = sum|e_t| / sum|y_t| over the horizon, division-by-zero problem of per-step actual-based scaling on intermittent series and the zero-error problem of benchmark-scaled measures: all found; unchanged. Relevance matches SPEC 7.3; 'zero-heavy' replaced by a computed figure. Strongly relevant.

title: Forecasting seasonals and trends by exponentially weighted moving averages
abstract_evidence: Publisher abstract (ScienceDirect page, fetched directly): the paper provides a systematic development of the forecasting expressions for exponentially weighted moving averages; methods for series with no trend or with additive or multiplicative trend are examined, and the methods cover non-seasonal and seasonal series with additive or multiplicative error structures. The paper is a reprinted version of the 1957 report to the Office of Naval Research (ONR 52), published to provide greater accessibility. Gardner (2006, Sec. 2) independently states that Holt's ONR memorandum developed exponential smoothing of additive trends and a separate method for smoothing seasonal data, and went unpublished until 2004.

title: A comparative study of various statistical and machine learning models for predicting restaurant demand in Bangladesh
abstract_evidence: Using historical sales data from a restaurant in Bangladesh, the study forecasts five selected products with two statistical and three machine-learning models, and ranks the models by their average deviation from the optimal root mean squared error. The Multilayer Perceptron and Random Forest took the top two positions, while the statistical models (simple exponential smoothing and Croston's method) outperformed XGBoost. The authors frame the work as improving demand forecasting for inventory management and fewer stock-outs in Bangladesh's restaurant industry.
relevance: Bab 2 penelitian terkait & Bab 3: supports benchmarking Takar's ML forecaster against simple statistical baselines (exponential smoothing, seasonal naive). In this restaurant study, ML models (Multilayer Perceptron, Random Forest) ranked first and second, but simple exponential smoothing and Croston's method beat XGBoost, so a boosted-tree model is not guaranteed to beat statistical methods on restaurant sales. Paper: related work on restaurant demand forecasting.

title: Why and how is Scrum being adapted in practice: A systematic review
abstract_evidence: This systematic review analyses literature reporting why and how Scrum, described as the most popular agile development methodology, was modified when used in non-traditional settings and for different needs. abstract_evidence: Crossref/OpenAlex abstract: the study is an in-depth life-cycle assessment of 'Foodforecast', an ML cloud service designed to reduce food waste in bakeries by optimising sales forecasting. It covers global warming, abiotic resource depletion, cumulative energy demand and freshwater eutrophication, including both the direct impacts of the ML model and hardware and the indirect benefits of avoided bakery returns compared with traditional ordering. According to sales reports, the service led to an average 30% reduction in bakery returns (mainly bread and rolls) in 2022, and the environmental benefits outweighed the direct impacts by one to three orders of magnitude. Support activities such as service maintenance were major direct impact factors, surpassing cloud compute for ML operations; within the compute, data processing and inference dominated and ML training played a minor role. The authors note that the results are constrained by methodological challenges and data uncertainties.

abstract_evidence: This review covers compositional and processing factors affecting the foaming properties of milk, noting that milk foams are desirable for cappuccino-style beverages. title: Another look at measures of forecast accuracy
abstract_evidence: Published abstract (ScienceDirect; same text on the author's publication page): discusses and compares measures of accuracy of univariate time-series forecasts; the measures used in the M-competition and the M3-competition, and many measures recommended by previous authors, are found to be degenerate in commonly occurring situations; proposes that the mean absolute scaled error (MASE) become the standard measure for comparing forecast accuracy across multiple time series. The author's full-text version (mase.pdf) adds that percentage-error measures such as MAPE are infinite or undefined when an actual value is zero (so they cannot be used for small-count/intermittent data), and that the scaled error is independent of the scale of the data and always defined and finite except when all historical observations are equal.
relevance: Bab 3 metode evaluasi, Bab 4 pembahasan, paper evaluation: justifies reporting MASE (scale-free and defined when actual sales are zero) next to MAE/RMSE when comparing Holt-Winters against ML forecasters across menu items and ingredients with different units; supports not relying on MAPE for low-volume items.

title: System Usability Scale Benchmarking for Digital Health Apps: Meta-analysis
abstract_evidence: A meta-analysis of 117 SUS scores for 114 digital health apps (DHAs) from papers published 2011-2021 tested whether the widely used SUS benchmark distribution (mean 68, SD 12.5) can reliably assess DHA usability. All apps averaged 76.64 (SD 15.12), a skewed, non-normal distribution driven by physical-activity apps (mean 83.28); excluding them, the mean was 68.05 (SD 14.05), not significantly different from the standard distribution (1-sample, 2-tailed t test, P = .98). The authors conclude that the SUS and the benchmark mean of 68 (SD 12.5) are suitable for evaluating the usability of DHAs and propose a template for reporting mean SUS scores.
relevance: Bab 4 pembahasan: comparing the PWA's mean SUS with the commonly used benchmark of 68 (SD 12.5), which this meta-analysis found suitable for digital health apps; Bab 3: reporting SUS with the proposed template (Textbox 1: participant type, context, n, mean (SD), median (min/max), SE, 95% CI, test used, SUS grade); paper evaluation section. Moderate relevance: the evidence is for digital health apps, not food-service or staff tools, so present it as support for using the benchmark, not as a domain-specific norm.

title: Systems and software engineering — Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Product quality model
abstract_evidence: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 (Edition 2, published 2023-11, 22 pages, committee ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 7) replaces the withdrawn ISO/IEC 25010:2011 and defines a product quality model applicable to ICT and software products. title: Session-aware recommendation: A surprising quest for the state-of-the-art
abstract_evidence: Benchmarks recent session-aware recommendation algorithms against each other and against session-based algorithms and heuristic extensions; simple nearest-neighbour techniques consistently outperform recent neural techniques and session-aware models were mostly not better than approaches without long-term preference information. The open-access author version (arXiv:2011.03424v2) states that when only the immediate next item is the target 'the used metrics are the Hit Rate (HR) and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR)', that 'Coverage tells us how many items actually ever appear in the top-n lists of users' (also known as aggregate diversity), and that popularity bias is the average min-max-normalised training popularity of the recommended items; its result tables report MAP@20, P@20, R@20, HR@20, MRR@20, COV@20 and POP@20.
relevance: Bab 2/Bab 3 metode evaluasi and paper method: recent peer-reviewed benchmark that uses HR and MRR for next-item evaluation and reports them together with catalogue coverage (aggregate diversity) and popularity bias, and shows that simple nearest-neighbour heuristics are strong baselines, which supports comparing FP-Growth rules with popularity and co-occurrence baselines. It gives no HR/MRR formulas (use deshpande2004itembased for those) and does not define the SPEC's 'query coverage' (share of test queries in which at least one rule fires); define that as the thesis's own measure. Its domain is session-based/session-aware recommendation, not association rules.
topic: HR@k, MRR@k and coverage in session-based recommendation evaluation

title: Optimizing Raw Material Inventory for Culinary MSMEs under Data Scarcity: A DR-ARMA Forecasting Approach
abstract_evidence: Targets culinary MSMEs whose raw materials perish quickly and whose daily demand fluctuates, where sparse, intermittent sales records defeat data-hungry forecasting tools. It proposes DR-ARMA, which extends classical ARMA in three stages - baseline ARIMA modelling, moving-average trend detection, and adaptive calibration that feeds forecast errors directly into safety-stock computation via an RMSE-buffered adjustment. On a three-month daily sales dataset (90 observations, over 30% zero-sales days) from an Indonesian culinary business it reached MAPE 24.64% versus 42.70% for simple moving average and 24.99% for the naive benchmark; the safety-stock buffer gave an empirical 80% service level, and the model was embedded in a desktop system producing daily procurement lists.
relevance: Bab 2 penelitian terkait & Bab 3 metode; paper related work: closest Indonesian precedent for coupling short-history demand forecasts with forecast-error-based safety stock to output daily purchase lists for perishable ingredients - directly comparable to the proposed restock recommendation; also illustrates zero-inflated daily sales typical of small outlets.

title: Barista Diary: An autoethnography studying the operational experience of third-wave coffee shop baristas
abstract_evidence: Autoethnography of the day-to-day operational experiences of baristas in the third-wave coffee sector during the Covid-19 pandemic, built from personal memory mining, observational fieldnotes, focus groups, interviews and storytelling. Shows how baristas develop skills as habitual powers, manage operational chaos through aesthetic experience and turn simple coffeemaking into hospitality. Concludes that a barista's job is a nexus of intricacies beyond just making coffee that often goes undiscussed in academia and practice.

title: Uneven extraction in coffee brewing
abstract_evidence: Motivated by an experiment showing that, beyond a cutoff, grinding coffee more finely lowers extraction, the authors derive and analyse a low-dimensional model with two possible flow pathways through the coffee bed. Below a critical grind size the model reproduces decreasing extraction with decreasing grind size, as seen experimentally. This arises from an initial imbalance in porosities and permeabilities of the two pathways that flow and extraction amplify, leading to complete extraction of all soluble coffee from one pathway.

Bab 3 sistem pakar: dasar kehati-hatian untuk aturan 'giling lebih halus' pada seduhan under-extracted (menurut model, di bawah ukuran gilingan kritis ekstraksi justru turun); bersifat teoretis tanpa ambang numerik. Paper related work (Physics of Fluids).

title: An equilibrium desorption model for the strength and extraction yield of full immersion brewed coffee
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract_evidence: A pseudo-equilibrium desorption model predicts that, for full-immersion coffee, TDS is approximately inversely proportional to the water/coffee brew ratio while extraction yield (E) is independent of the brew ratio; experiments agreed, with E approximately 21% over a wide range of brew ratios. The equilibrium constant was insensitive to grind size, roast level and brew temperature over 80–99 °C, and the standard oven-drying method was shown to underestimate E at equilibrium. The authors conclude practitioners should pay careful attention to brew ratio as the most important parameter for full-immersion brewing.

Bab 3 perancangan kalkulator skala resep dinamis: dasar kuantitatif (untuk seduhan imersi penuh) bahwa TDS kira-kira berbanding terbalik dengan rasio air:kopi sedangkan EY tidak bergantung pada rasio, sehingga penskalaan ukuran/jumlah cangkir mempertahankan rasio tetap (mis. 1:15) agar kekuatan seduhan tetap; untuk V60 (perkolasi) hanya pendekatan. Paper method: justification of the ratio-preserving recipe-scaling formula.

title: Kadar Bioaktif dan Aktivitas Antioksidan Seduhan Kopi Arabika dengan Variasi Metode Penyeduhan

title: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
abstract_evidence: RFC 9700 (BCP 240) describes best current security practice for OAuth 2.0: it updates and extends the threat model and security advice of RFCs 6749, 6750 and 6819 with practical experience gathered since OAuth 2.0 was published, covers new threats arising from the broader application of OAuth 2.0, and deprecates modes of operation deemed less secure or even insecure. Section 2.4 states that the resource owner password credentials grant MUST NOT be used, because it insecurely exposes the resource owner's credentials to the client, increases the attack surface, trains users to enter their credentials in places other than the authorization server, and is not designed to work with two-factor authentication or multi-step authentication processes. Section 2.1.1 requires public clients to use PKCE with the authorization code grant.
relevance: Bab 2 Tinjauan Referensi and Bab 5 Simpulan dan Saran (keterbatasan dan saran): current OAuth 2.0 security guidance; because it says the password credentials grant MUST NOT be used, Takar's first-party password login (FastAPI OAuth2 password form) is reported as a prototype limitation, and the authorization code grant with PKCE (or a hardened session design) is proposed as future work. Paper: limitations.

title: Evaluating the impact of caching on the energy consumption and performance of progressive web apps
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 7th International Conference on Mobile Software Engineering and Systems
abstract_evidence: An empirical experiment on 9 real third-party PWAs, designed as 1 factor (caching) with 2 treatments (empty vs populated cache), executed on a real Android device with Mozilla Firefox and measuring device energy consumption and page load time. title: Impact of the human factor on the reproducibility of different coffee brewing methods
venue: Journal of Food Composition and Analysis
abstract_evidence: Noting that most filter methods are time-consuming and dependent on the skill of the operator/barista, the study had six expert baristas each prepare a medium-roasted specialty coffee with four filter methods (Pure Brew, V60, AeroPress and French Press) to understand the influence of the human factor on preparation. title: Coffee Value Assessment: Sample Preparation and Tasting Mechanics
abstract_evidence: The SCA standard defines sample preparation and tasting mechanics for the Coffee Value Assessment (designed for green Coffea arabica) and supersedes the heritage SCA cupping standards and the SCA Cupping Protocol (2004 and any later editions). It specifies a cupping-level (medium) roast with ground-coffee L* of 26–29 (approximately Agtron/SCA tile #65), a dose of 8.25 g coffee per 150 mL of vessel capacity (tolerance ±0.2 g), a grind with 70–75% passing a 20-mesh (850 µm) sieve, water at 93 ± 3 °C, and five cups per sample for affective assessment; cupping water should contain no chlorine, with calcium hardness 50–175 ppm CaCO3, alkalinity at or near 40–70 ppm CaCO3 and pH 6–8. For batch-brewed descriptive assessment it recommends 55–60 g of coffee per litre of water (approximately 17:1 to 18:1 water-to-coffee). The standard states that abbreviated cupping of many samples for quality-control or quick decision-making purposes is outside its scope.
relevance: Bab 2 landasan teori: contoh standar resmi industri (SCA) yang menetapkan parameter persiapan secara kuantitatif (tingkat sangrai, rasio kopi:air, gilingan, suhu dan spesifikasi air) sebagai analogi 'standarisasi operasional'; spesifikasi air (tanpa klorin, kesadahan kalsium 50–175 ppm CaCO3, alkalinitas sekitar 40–70 ppm CaCO3, pH 6–8) dapat dirujuk di modul SOP. Catatan: parameter tersebut untuk cupping/penilaian nilai kopi, bukan resep minuman bar (mis. V60 1:15), dan standar ini menyatakan cupping ringkas untuk kontrol mutu berada di luar cakupannya. title: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation
abstract_evidence: Crossref abstract: deep-learning based generation 'is prone to hallucinate unintended text, which degrades the system performance and fails to meet user expectations in many real-world scenarios'; the survey gives an overview of metrics, mitigation methods and future directions, and of task-specific progress in abstractive summarization, dialogue generation, generative question answering, data-to-text generation and machine translation. Definitions (author version, Section 2): 'Intrinsic Hallucinations: The generated output that contradicts the source content' and 'Extrinsic Hallucinations: The generated output that cannot be verified from the source content (i.e., output that can neither be supported nor contradicted by the source)'; extrinsic hallucination 'is still treated with caution because its unverifiable aspect of this additional information increases the risk from a factual safety perspective'.
relevance: Bab 2 landasan teori (definition and types of hallucination) and Bab 3 metric design: Takar's numeric-hallucination rate counts numbers in the answer that appear in neither the question, the retrieved context nor the tool outputs - numbers that 'cannot be verified from the source content', i.e. extrinsic hallucination in Ji et al.'s sense, applied to quantities. A number that contradicts a tool result or chunk (intrinsic hallucination) is counted only if that number appears nowhere in the sources, so the metric neither separates the two types nor catches every contradiction; state this, or check contradictions against the tool outputs separately. Cited again in Bab 4 when comparing closed-book, RAG and RAG + tools, and in the paper's evaluation section.

title: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models: Principles, Taxonomy, Challenges, and Open Questions
abstract_evidence: Crossref abstract: 'LLMs are prone to hallucination, generating plausible yet nonfactual content', which raises concerns over their reliability in real-world information retrieval systems; the survey proposes a taxonomy of hallucination for the LLM era, reviews contributing factors, detection methods and benchmarks, mitigation methods, and 'the current limitations faced by retrieval-augmented LLMs in combating hallucinations'. title: RAGAs: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
venue: Proceedings of the 18th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: System Demonstrations
abstract_evidence: Introduces RAGAs (Retrieval Augmented Generation Assessment), 'a framework for reference-free evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines'. RAG systems 'provide LLMs with knowledge from a reference textual database, enabling them to act as a natural language layer between a user and textual databases, thus reducing the risk of hallucinations'; evaluation must cover 'the ability of the retrieval system to identify relevant and focused context passages, the ability of the LLM to exploit such passages faithfully, and the quality of the generation itself'. Full text: three quality aspects - faithfulness ('the answer should be grounded in the given context'; an answer is faithful 'if the claims that are made in the answer can be inferred from the context', scored F = |V|/|S|, the share of LLM-extracted statements the LLM judges supported), answer relevance (whose assessment 'does not take into account factuality'; the LLM generates questions from the answer and their text-embedding-ada-002 cosine similarity to the original question is averaged) and context relevance (which 'aims to penalise the inclusion of redundant information'); 'all prompts are evaluated using the gpt-3.5-turbo-16k model', and agreement with human judgements is analysed on the new WikiEval dataset.
relevance: Bab 2/3 (dimensions of RAG evaluation) and paper evaluation design. Takar covers analogous, not identical, aspects: retrieval (BM25 Recall@1/3/5 and MRR against gold chunks - whether the right chunk is found, whereas RAGAs' context relevance scores how focused the context is), grounding (the numeric-hallucination rate, a number-only proxy for faithfulness) and answer correctness (all required facts present - which RAGAs' answer relevance explicitly does not assess). Takar uses deterministic reference-based checks against author-built gold facts instead of RAGAs' reference-free LLM-judge prompts, which would need a cloud LLM (gpt-3.5-turbo-16k in the paper) and add judge variance; state this choice and its limitation.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
abstract_evidence: RAG 'is a promising approach for mitigating the hallucination of large language models', but its impact on different LLMs lacked rigorous evaluation. The authors analyse '4 fundamental abilities required for RAG, including noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness', build the Retrieval-Augmented Generation Benchmark (RGB) in English and Chinese, and evaluate 6 LLMs: 'while LLMs exhibit a certain degree of noise robustness, they still struggle significantly in terms of negative rejection, information integration, and dealing with false information'. Full text: negative rejection means an LLM 'should reject to answer the question when the required knowledge is not present in any retrieved document'; accuracy uses exact matching - 'if the generated text contains an exact match to the answer, it is considered as a correct answer'; 'The highest rejection rates for LLMs in English and Chinese were only 45% and 43.33%, respectively'.
relevance: Bab 2 and Bab 3 evaluation design, paper evaluation section: RGB's negative rejection is the basis of Takar's 'di luar cakupan' category and refusal-accuracy metric (the system prompt tells the model to say it does not know when the context lacks the answer), and its contains-the-answer exact-match scoring parallels Takar's 'all required facts present' rule. The low rejection rates it reports motivate testing refusal explicitly rather than trusting the prompt instruction.

title: Large Language Models Only Pass Primary School Exams in Indonesia: A Comprehensive Test on IndoMMLU
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
abstract_evidence: LLMs are 'often pre-trained on large-scale multilingual texts', but 'their reasoning abilities and real-world knowledge are mainly evaluated based on English datasets'. IndoMMLU is 'the first multi-task language understanding benchmark for Indonesian culture and languages', with questions from primary school to university entrance exams: 14,981 questions across 64 tasks and education levels written with professional teachers, 46% of them on Indonesian language proficiency and nine local languages and cultures. 'GPT-3.5 only manages to pass the Indonesian primary school level, with limited knowledge of local Indonesian languages and culture', and smaller models such as BLOOMZ and Falcon perform even lower.
